articles.title: एनसेल अब सरकारको नाममा आउने, सर्वोच्चको बोल्ड फैसलापछि वालेन्द्रको परीक्षा शुरु
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । एनसेल निजी क्षेत्रको अग्रणी सञ्चार माध्यमको रुपमा स्थापित कम्पनी हो। तर, एनसेलले नेपालमा गरिरहेको व्यापार र सेवा प्रवाह भने विवादास्पद नै छ। कर प्रकरणदेखि अन्य विषयमा समेत लम्बेतान विवादमा फसेको एनसेलको सेयर किनबेचपछि भने यसबारेका प्रश्नको सवालमा सर्वोच्च अदालतको आदेशपछि थप कानूनी प्रष्टतासहित अवैध गतिविधिविरुद्ध नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको कार्यान्वयन गर्न सक्षम छ भन्ने सन्देश दिएको छ ।

लामो समय कर विवादमा फसेको एनसेल नेपालको अग्रणी निजी क्षेत्रको टेलिकम सेवा प्रदायक बन्न पुग्यो। नेपालको टेलिकम क्षेत्रमा नविनताका निम्ति काम गरेको एनसेलले सञ्चारको क्षेत्रमा खेलेको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न गर्ने ठाउँ छैन्।

अझं भन्नुपर्दा सरकारी स्वामित्वको नेपाल टेलिकमले दिने सेवालाई एनसेलले दिएको चुनौतीकै कारण सञ्चार क्षेत्रले नेपालमा राम्रो स्तरको सेवा प्रवाहमा काम गरेको पाइन्छ। तर, एनसेलको यो राम्रो पाटोसंगै विवाद भने अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण छन्। हरेक वर्ष मनग्य आम्दानी पनि दिएको एनसेलले विदेशमा नोपलबाट ठूलो धनराशी पठाएको छ।

सेवासंगै मेवा पनि दिएको एनसेलले केहि विवाद यस्ता पनि भोग्यो, जुन नेपालको कानूनको प्रत्यक्ष उल्लङ्घन र राज्यविरुद्ध गरेको एकखाले अपराध नै हो। कर छली विवाद लामो समयसम्म लम्बिदा एनसेलले आफ्ना भौतिक संरचनामा क्षति व्यहोर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। अझं, तत्कालीन विप्लव नेतृत्वको नेकपाले एनसेलको कार्यालयमा बम विस्फोट गराएपछि सेक्युरिटी गार्डले ज्यान नै दिने स्थिति बन्यो। यसरी देशभरका विभिन्न क्षेत्रका भौतिक संरचनामा किन आक्रमण भए? यसका पछाडी कारण हुन्, एनसेलले नेपालको कानून पालना गर्न भन्दा बढि मुनाफा आर्जन गर्ने ध्येय राख्नु।

सेयर खरिदबिक्रीको घोटाला

एनसेलले गरेको सेयर खरिदबिक्री भने अस्वभाविकमात्रै थिएन, सार्वभौम मुलुकको स्वाधिनतामाथिको प्रहार नै थियो। नेपालले निर्माण गरेको कानून व्यवसायमैत्री थिएन भनेपनि त्यो कानून नेपालको सार्वभौमसत्तासंग जोडिएको विषय थियो।

नेपालको संसदले निर्माण गरेको कानून नेपालभित्र सबैलाई मान्य र बाध्यकारी हुन्छ। तर, एनसेलको हकमा यो लागू नहुने गरि गरिएको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीमा सर्वोच्चको झड्कापछि भने नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको पालना निर्वाध गराउनसक्छ भन्ने प्रष्ट सन्देश दिएको छ ।

सेयर खरिदबिक्री अमान्य

सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीशद्वय सपना प्रधान मल्ल र टेकप्रसाद ढुंगानाको संयुक्त इजलासले विवादास्पद सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भन्दै खारेज गरिदिएको छ।

यसले एनसेलको अध्यक्ष बन्न पुगेका सतिसलाल आचार्य अब कर्मचारीको हैसियतमा पुगेका छन भने एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व रेनोल्ड होल्डिङ्स लिमिटेडको वास्तविक मालिक मलेसियन कम्पनी आजियाटाकै रहेको ठहर गरेको छ। सतिसलालको कम्पनी स्पेक्ट्रलाइट युकेले किनेको भनिएको ८० प्रतिशत सेयर अमान्य भएको छ ।

के भन्यो सर्वोच्चले ?

सर्वोच्च अदालतले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व ६ अर्ब हाराहारीमा भएको कारोबारलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भनेको छ । अदालतले सन् २०१६ मा करिब १ खर्ब ४३ अर्ब रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरिएको शेयरलाई अत्यन्तै न्यून मूल्यमा किनबेच गरिएको भन्नुलाई नै कानूनको उल्लङ्घनको रुपमा ठहर गरेको हो। सर्वोच्चले आदेशमा भनेको छ, ’शेयर खरीद बिक्री कारोबारको बारेमा विदेशी लगानी तथा प्रविधि हस्तान्तरण ऐन, २०७५ को दफा १९ को अभिलेख राख्ने व्यवस्थासँग आफूलाई अनुमति दिने, नियमन गर्ने विशेष कानूनको रूपमा रहेको दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (१) (ट) को व्यवस्थालाई नजरअन्दाज गर्न मिल्ने देखिएन ।

प्रस्तुत संशोधित ऐ. नियम १५ ( १ ) (ट) तथा नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण ( अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ को विनियम (१), (३) र विनियम ४ को खण्ड (क) लाई चुनौति दिएको अवस्था पनि रहेको छैन । अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्ति विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको ८०% शेयर धारण गर्ने शेयरवाला आजियाटा इन्भेष्टमेन् (यु.के.) लिमिटेडले आफ्नो शेयर स्पेक्ट्रलाइट यु.के. लिमिटेडलाई मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार १ डिसेम्बर २०२३) मा बिक्री गरेको तथ्यमा विवाद देखिदैन । उक्त शेयर कारोवार हुनु अगावै नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट पूर्व स्वीकृति लिनुपर्नेमा नलिएको, विपक्षीबाट पेस भएको लिखित जवाफमा शेयरधनीको शेयर खरीद बिक्री हुँदा प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिनुपर्ने व्यवस्था नै छैन भन्ने जिकिर लिएको र मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार डिसेम्वर १ सन् २०२३) मा भएको शेयर खरीद बिक्री सम्झौताको सम्बन्धमा मिति २०८०।११।१२ मा मात्र स्वीकृतिको लागि प्राधिकरणमा निवेदन पेस गरेको स्थिति देखिएकाले विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडले दुर सञ्चार ऐन, २०५३, दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ र नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण (अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ र अनुमतिपत्रको शर्तसमेत अक्षरशः परिपालना गर्दै पारदर्शी र विधिसम्मत तरिकाले सेवा संचालन गर्नू भनी विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको नाममा निर्देशनात्मक आदेश जारी गरिदिएको छ ।’

यसरी हेर्दा अब एनसेलको सञ्चालन एनसेल आजियाटाले नै गर्नुपर्नेछ। यसरी हेर्दा सतिसलालले गरेको कारोबार अवैध ठहर भएको छ भने अब ससितलाल एनसेलको अध्यक्षभन्दा पनि कर्मचारी वा अन्य हैसियतमा पुग्ने भएका छन्।

अब सरकारीकरणको बाटो खुला

नेपालको दूरसञ्चार ऐनले निश्वित अवधिपछि निश्चित कानूनी बाटो पुरा नगरेमा टेलिकम कम्पनी नेपाल सरकारको नाममा स्वतः आउने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। जसअनुसार दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ को दफा ३३ अनुसार ५० प्रतिशतभन्दा बढी विदेशी लगानी भएका दूरसञ्चार कम्पनीहरूको अनुमतिपत्रको २५ वर्षे अवधि समाप्त भएपछि त्यसको स्वामित्व स्वतः नेपाल सरकारमा हस्तान्तरण हुने व्यवस्था गरेको छ ।

एनसेलले १६ भदौ २०६१ मा अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरेकाले १५ भदौ २०८६ मा यसको २५ वर्षे अवधि पुरा हुनेछ । जुन अवधिपछि एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्वमा वैध वदलाव नआएमा सरकारीकरणको चरणमा प्रवेश गर्ने निश्वित छ ।

उसोतः एनसेल प्रकरणमा नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआइबी)ले ठगी, आपराधिक विश्वासघात जस्ता विषयमा अनुसन्धान भने गरिरहेको छ। सर्वोच्चले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व सरकारको नाममा आउने बाटो खुला गरिदिएपनि कानूनी बाटाहरु कसरी अघि बढ्छन्? सरकारी नीति कस्ता बन्छन भन्ने विषयले समेत यो विषयमा थप निर्धारण गर्नेछ ।

अमरेशको सक्रियता

तत्कालीन समयमा स्वतन्त्र रुपमा प्रतिनिधिसभामा निर्वाचित भएका अमरेशकुमार सिंहले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई चुनौती दिदै सर्वोच्चमा रिट दर्ता गराए। अमरेश अहिले राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीबाट कांग्रेस सभापति गगन थापालाई पराजित गर्दै फेरि सर्लाही निर्वाचन क्षेत्र नम्बर ४ बाट प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्यमा निर्वाचित भइसकेका छन्।

उनै सिंहले सर्वोच्चमा एनसेल आजियाटा, दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण, प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय, ठूला करदाता कार्यालय, कम्पनी रजिष्ट्रार जस्ता धेरै निकायलाई विपक्षी बनाएर रिट दर्ता गराएका थिए। यहि प्रकरणमा सर्वोच्चको फैसलाले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अवैध ठहर गरेको हो।

निर्णय अब सरकारको हातमा

नेपालमा विदेशी लगानीका सम्बन्धमा अनेक अफवाहहरु फैलिने गर्छन्। कतिपयले एनसेल प्रकरणले नेपालमा ठूला लगानी नआउने भन्दै यसलाई मोड्ने प्रयास समेत गरेको देखिन्छ। सरकारले पनि मध्यम वर्गलाई ठूलो प्रभाव पर्ने गरि काम गरिरहेको बेला विदेशी लगानीलाई नेपालको कानूनको पालना गर्ने र विवादको समाधानका निम्ति सहजीकरणको बाटो खोज्दै काम गर्ने वातावरण सिर्जना गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ ।

एनसेल कब्जा गर्ने सतिसलालसहितको टोलीले नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा लिलाम सकारेको घटनाबाटै सरकारले कानूनको पालना गराउने र आवश्यक सहजीकरणसहित दण्ड र पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गर्न आवश्यक देखिन्छ। तर, सरकारले यस्ता विषयलाई कसरी अघि लैजान्छ भन्ने चासो र केहि शंकाहरु भने देखिन्छन। यद्यपी अब कानूनविपरितका विषयलाई दण्ड र विदेशी लगानीलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्ने गरि काम गर्नुको विकल्प भने देखिन्न ।

articles.title: कोलकाताबाट २४ घण्टामै नेपालमा ढुवानी, व्यवसायी उत्साहित
articles.summary:
मोरङ । उद्घाटन भएको करिब ३ वर्षपछि विराटनगरस्थित एकीकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधन पछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपालको कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो ।

विराटनगर स्थित एकिकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । तत्कालिन प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल प्रचण्ड र भारतका प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीले २०८० साल जेठ १८ गते उद्घाटन गरेयता कार्गो रेल आउन सकेको थिएन ।

मोरङको नेमुवास्थित स्वस्तिक आयल इण्डष्ट्रिजले मगाएको तोरी बोकेका ४० वटा कन्टेनरसहितको कार्गो रेल नेपाल भंसार यार्डसम्म आएको हो । रेल आएपछि सुनसरी मोरङ औद्योगिक करिडोरका उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरु उत्साहित भएका छन् ।

कार्गो रेलबाट ढुवानी गर्दा ढुवानी लागत २५ देखि ३० प्रतिशत घट्ने, कोलकाता बन्दरगाहबाट विराटनगरसम्म २४ घण्टामा सामान आईपुग्ने र बाटोमा सामान चोरी हुने समस्या निराकरण हुने भएकाले अन्य क्षेत्रका उद्योगहरुसँग प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्न सहज हुने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

भारत सरकार अन्र्तर्गतको कन्कोर अर्थात कन्टेनर कर्पोरेशन अफ इण्डिया लिमिटेडको कार्गाे रेलबाट सोमवार एनसिवाई अर्थात नेपाल कस्टम यार्ड सम्म मालवाहक रेल आएको हो ।

कन्कोरका प्रतिनिधि संजिव साहले हप्तामा दुई दिन कोलकाताबाट विराटनगरसम्म कार्गो रेल संचालन गर्ने र यसलाई आवश्यकता अनुसार बढाउदै लैजाने जानकारी दिए ।

पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधनपछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपाल कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो । कार्गो रेल संचालन पछि विराटनगर आएको कन्टेनर खाली फर्कने भएकाले यहाँबाट वस्तु निर्यातमा पनि सहजता आउने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

articles.title: प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालद्वारा ‘Soirée Francaise’ आयोजना: फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति र जीवनशैलीको अनुभव
articles.summary:
अग्नि ग्रुप अन्तर्गतको प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालले ‘Soirée Française – A Night of French Elegance’ शीर्षकमा एक विशेष 'फ्रेन्च फाइन डाइनिङ' कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न गरेको छ। काठमाडौँस्थित ला टेरास (La Terrasse) मा आयोजना गरिएको उक्त कार्यक्रममा प्युजोका विशिष्ट ग्राहक, व्यावसायिक साझेदार तथा फ्रान्सेली संस्कृतिप्रति आत्मियता राख्ने अतिथिहरूको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो।

कार्यक्रमले फ्रान्सको समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक विरासत र त्यसको प्रेरणादायी भावनालाई सम्मान गर्दै आपसी सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने उद्देश्य राखेको थियो।

विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीको भावनाबाट प्रेरित

सन् २०२६ को फिफा विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीले प्रदर्शन गरेको समर्पण, दृढता, उत्कृष्टता र एकताको भावनाबाट प्रेरित भई यो कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरिएको हो। खेलको नतिजाभन्दा माथि उठेर फ्रान्सेली खेल संस्कृतिको अदम्य भावना र त्यसको विरासतलाई सम्मान गर्नु कार्यक्रमको मुख्य पक्ष थियो। यी मूल्यहरू प्युजो ब्रान्डको दीर्घकालीन पहिचानसँग समेत मेल खाने भएकाले सोही भावनालाई कार्यक्रममा प्रतिबिम्बित गरिएको थियो।

नेटवर्किङ र प्रिमियम जीवनशैलीको अनुभव

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी अतिथिहरूले पेरिस-प्रेरित आकर्षक सजावट तथा आत्मीय वातावरणमा विविध परम्परागत फ्रेन्च परिकारको स्वाद लिँदै नेटवर्किङको अनुभव सँगालेका थिए। प्युजोको फ्रान्सेली सम्पदालाई झल्काउँदै आफ्ना ग्राहकहरूप्रति कृतज्ञता व्यक्त गर्न र नेपालमा प्युजो समुदायसँगको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउन यस अवसरले सहयोग पुर्‍याएको कम्पनीले जनाएको छ।

ग्राहक केन्द्रित प्रतिबद्धता

यस अवसरमा प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूले गुणस्तरीय गतिशीलता (मोबिलिटी) समाधानका साथै ग्राहकलाई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरको जीवनशैली अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने र विश्वव्यापी रूपमा प्युजोले प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने मूल्य एवम् परम्परालाई निरन्तर अघि बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता पुनः व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रमको समापन फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति, मित्रता र उत्कृष्टताको साझा भावनाप्रति सम्मान व्यक्त गर्दै ‘टोस्ट’ (Toast) का साथ गरिएको थियो। सहभागीहरूले यस अविस्मरणीय अनुभवले प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपाल र ग्राहकहरूबीचको प्रिमियम सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाएको विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन्

articles.title: राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस घोषणा गर्न इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनको माग
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनका अध्यक्ष सुवासचन्द्र बरालले प्रत्येक वर्ष साउन ३ गते मनाइने इन्जिनियर दिवसलाई सरकारले औपचारिक रूपमा ‘राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस’ घोषणा गरी सरकारी क्यालेन्डरमा समावेश गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

एसोसियसनको ६४औँ इन्जिनियर दिवस समारोहलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै अध्यक्ष बरालले पूर्वाधार र प्रविधि कुनै पनि राष्ट्रको आर्थिक विकास र समृद्धिको मेरुदण्ड भएको उल्लेख गर्दै इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेर राज्यले दीर्घकालीन नीति अवलम्बन गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

उनका अनुसार नेपालमा दर्ता भएका करिब एक लाख इन्जिनियरमध्ये करिब ६० प्रतिशत युवा छन्। तर पर्याप्त रोजगारी र अवसरको अभावका कारण ठूलो संख्यामा दक्ष जनशक्ति विदेश पलायन भइरहेको भन्दै उनले यसलाई रोक्न तत्काल प्रभावकारी नीति आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

‘युवा इन्जिनियरहरूको सीप, ज्ञान र दक्षताको उचित उपयोग गर्न राज्य, उद्योग र इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायबीच बलियो सहकार्य आवश्यक छ,’ उनले भने।

बरालले यस वर्षको इन्जिनियर दिवस 'Young Mind and Engineering: Shaping Better Nepal' भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइएको जानकारी दिँदै विकास निर्माणमा संलग्न प्राविधिकहरूले कार्यस्थलमा असुरक्षा, प्रशासनिक झन्झट र अनावश्यक दबाब झेल्नुपरेको गुनासो गरे। यस्तो अवस्थाले विकास आयोजनाको गति नै प्रभावित भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनले प्राविधिकहरूको क्षमताको अधिकतम उपयोग गर्न पुरस्कार र दण्डको स्पष्ट प्रणाली लागू गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औँल्याए। ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत, कृषि, पर्यटन, सूचना प्रविधि, उद्योग तथा मानव संसाधनलगायत सबै क्षेत्रमा इन्जिनियरहरूको भूमिका निर्णायक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै बदलिँदो प्रविधिअनुसार सीप विकासमा लगानी बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

सरकारसमक्ष एसोसियसनले इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न नीतिगत माग पनि अघि सारेको छ।

अध्यक्ष बरालले विकास निर्माणमा खटिने इन्जिनियरका लागि सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरणको कानुनी प्रत्याभूति, रणनीतिक सरकारी निकायको नेतृत्व तहमा प्राविधिक पृष्ठभूमिका इन्जिनियरहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व, छुट्टै इन्जिनियरिङ सेवा आयोग गठन तथा नेपाल इन्जिनियरिङ प्रशिक्षण तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाउन आग्रह गरे।

त्यसैगरी, युवा इन्जिनियरका लागि पर्याप्त रोजगारी सिर्जना, विकास आयोजनाको सुपरभिजन इन्जिनियरबाटै गराउने व्यवस्था, निजी तथा गैरसरकारी क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत इन्जिनियरहरूको न्यूनतम मासिक पारिश्रमिक ३७ हजार १३५ कार्यान्वयन तथा प्राविधिक त्रुटिलाई स्वतः भ्रष्टाचारको कसुर अन्तर्गत नराख्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्न पनि उनले सरकारसँग माग गरे।

अध्यक्ष बरालले नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसन इन्जिनियरहरूको पेशागत हकहितको संरक्षण, नवप्रवर्तनको प्रवर्द्धन र राज्यसँग इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायलाई जोड्ने साझा संस्थाका रूपमा निरन्तर सक्रिय रहने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गर्दै सम्पूर्ण इन्जिनियर तथा आर्किटेक्टलाई पेशागत नैतिकता र इमान्दारितालाई सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकतामा राखेर समृद्ध नेपाल निर्माणमा योगदान दिन आह्वान गरे।

articles.title: जेनजी आन्दोलन प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गत वर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गते देशमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोह र त्यसक्रममा भएका गम्भीर मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटनासम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ पुगेको छ ।

नेपालभित्र प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न चौतर्फी माग भइरहेका बेला आयोगले करिब १० हजार पृष्ठ लामो उक्त प्रतिवेदन जेनेभास्थित मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा पेश गरेको छ।

तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली र गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखकसहित उच्च अधिकारीहरूमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धानको सिफारिस गरिएको यो प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पुगेसँगै अब सरकारमाथि कूटनीतिक र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढ्ने देखिएको छ ।

गएको भदौ २३–२४ गतेको जेनजी विद्रोहसम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय मानव अधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय ओएचसीएचआर जेनेभामा पेश भएको छ ।

यो प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अब सरकारलाई थप दबाब पर्नेछ । जुन १५ देखि जुलाइ ७ सम्म जेनेभामा चलेको ह्युमन राइट काउन्सिलको २४औँ बैठक र ६२ औँ सत्रमा राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगका सदस्य मिहिर ठाकुरले नेपालमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोहको मानवअधिकार अवस्थाका विस्तृत विवरणसहितको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि सरकारलाई बुझाएको जानकारी दिँदै सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वय गर्नैपर्ने जानकारी गराएका थिए ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगले पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनलाई नोटमा राखेको छ । सरकारलाई मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अरु दबाब पर्नेछ । जेनेभा बैठकमा भाग लिन आयोगका सदस्य ठाकुरसँगै आयोगकी उपसचिव माया शर्मा पनि पुगेकी थिइन ।

सरकारमाथि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढाउने रणनीति

आयोगभित्रैका केही अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगर्ने आशंका बढेपछि आयोगले प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पठाएको हो ।

नेपालमै प्रतिवेदन पूर्णरूपमा सार्वजनिक गर्न आग्रह मानव अधिकार आयोगले आग्रह गरे पनि त्यो सम्भव नभएको बताउने गरेकाले पनि अब जेनेभाबाटै थप प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढ्न सक्ने अवस्था बनेको छ ।

प्रतिवेदनमा को–कोमाथि अनुसन्धान सिफारिस ?

जेनजी आन्दोलनमा भएको दमन, गोली प्रहार, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी तथा विध्वंसका घटनाबारे आयेगको प्रतिवेदन करिब १० हजार पृष्ठको छ । तर आयोगले प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश मात्रै सार्वजनिक गरेको थियो ।

उक्त प्रतिवेदनमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली, तत्कालीन गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखक, तत्कालीन सञ्चारमन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङ, तत्कालीन प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक चन्द्रकुवेर खापुङ लगायतमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएको छ ।

यसैगरी आन्दोलनका क्रममा भएको विध्वंसमा कलाकार, पत्रकार, इन्फ्लुएन्सर तथा हाल संसद् र सरकारमा रहेका केही व्यक्तिहरूमाथि पनि थप अनुसन्धान गर्न आयोगले सिफारिस गरेको छ ।

आन्दोलनका घटनाबारे आयोगको निष्कर्ष

पूर्ण प्रतिवेदनमा भदौ २३ देखि २६ सम्मका घटना समेटिएका छन् । कसले कोसँग संवाद ग¥यो ?के–के कुरा भयो ? सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगो लगाउनेसम्ममा कसको योजना थियो भन्ने समेटिएका छन् ।

भीड कसरी उग्र बन्यो, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी गर्ने योजना कसरी बनेको थियो भन्ने विवरण पनि प्रतिवेदनमा समावेश छ । आयोगले अनुसन्धानका लागि आवश्यक केही प्रमाण, विशेषगरी गोलीका अवशेष बुलेट संकलन गर्न नसकिएको स्वीकार गरेको छ ।

ओली–लेखकले नै मागेका छन्, प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि

आयोगको पूर्ण प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न माग भइरहँदा फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएका पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री एवम् एमाले अध्यक्ष ओली, पूर्व गृहमन्त्री एवम् कांग्रेस नेता रमेश लेखक, पूर्व सञ्चार मन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङले प्रतिवेदनमाथि प्रश्न उठाउँदै आयोगसमक्ष निवेदन दर्ता गराएका छन् ।

प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश झिकिएको र केही अंश थपिएको आशंकापछि उनीहरुले प्रतिवेदन माग गरेका हुन् । ओलीको तर्फबाट छानबिन तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदन माग गर्दै एमाले नेता महेश बर्तौलाले असार १२ गते आयोगमा निवेदन दर्ता गराएका थिए ।

ओलीले आयोगको बैठकको निर्णय नम्बर १७७ को प्रमाणित प्रतिलिपि, लिली थापा नेतृत्वको समितिले आयोगमा पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि, प्रतिवेदनमा थपघट गरिएको अंश र थपघट गर्नुको कारणसमेत माग गरेका छन् ।

यस्तै, रास्वपा सभापति रवि लामिछानेलाई कारागारबाट बाहिर निकाल्न गएको आरोप लागेका सांसद दीपक बोहोराले पनि आयोगमा निवेदन दिएका थिए । आयोगले भनेको समयमा आफू अस्पतालमा रहेको उनको दलिल छ ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा प्रतिवेदन पेश भएपछि के हुन्छ ?

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले अब चार चरणमा प्रक्रिया अघि बढाउँछ ।

पहिलो चरण : अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अभिलेखः–

प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको आधिकारिक अभिलेखमा दर्ता हुन्छ । यसले नेपालमा मानव अधिकार उल्लंघन भएको दाबी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय निगरानीमा प्रवेश गर्छ ।

दोस्रो चरण : प्रश्न र स्पष्टीकरणः–

मानव अधिकार परिषद्का सदस्य राष्ट्रहरूले नेपाल सरकारसँग स्पष्टीकरण माग्न सक्छन् ।

तेस्रो चरण : सिफारिसः–

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय वा विशेष प्रतिवेदकहरूले नेपाललाई अनुसन्धान, पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति वा जिम्मेवार व्यक्तिमाथि कारबाही गर्न सिफारिस गर्न सक्छन् ।

चौथो चरण : निगरानीः–

नेपालले ती सिफारिस कार्यान्वयन ग¥यो कि गरेन भनेर आगामी सत्रहरूमा पुनःसमीक्षा हुन्छ ।

जेनजी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा दबाब

जेनजी आन्दोलनको प्रतिवेदन अब नेपालको आन्तरिक राजनीतिक विवाद मात्र रहेन, अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार बहसको विषय बनेको छ । मानव अधिकार परिषद्को ६२औँ सत्रमा यसबारे औपचारिक जानकारी प्रस्तुत भइसकेकाले नेपाल सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेमा आगामी सत्रहरूमा थप प्रश्न उठ्न सक्छन् ।

यद्यपी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेकै कारण कुनै देशलाई तुरुन्त प्रतिबन्ध भने लाग्दैन ।तर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आलोचना बढ्छ । मानव अधिकार सम्बन्धी वार्षिक प्रतिवेदनमा नकारात्मक उल्लेख हुन्छ । यसको असरले वैदेशिक सहायता र विकास साझेदारहरूको दबाब बढ्न सक्छ ।

त्यस्तै, विशेष प्रतिवेदक वा अनुसन्धान टोली पठाउने सम्भावना पनि रहन्छ। नेपालमा विगतमा द्वन्द्वकालीन मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका विषयमा संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघले पटक–पटक चासो व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

यस्ता घटनामा कुन कुन देशलाई प्रतिबन्ध लागेको छ ?

मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका आधारमा विभिन्न देशहरूमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको उदाहरणहरु छन् । म्यानमारमा सैन्य दमन र मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनको घटनामा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ भने इरानमा प्रदर्शनकारीमाथि दमन गरेको भन्दै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघन भएको निश्कर्षमा प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ।

त्यस्तै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटना छानबिन गरेर कारवाही नगरेका कारण बेलारुस, गृहयुद्ध र मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका कारण सिरिया लगायतका देश प्रतिबन्धमा परेका छन् ।

articles.title: झापाका ४२ परिवार तनावमा, अन्तिम किस्ता रोकिएपछि छटपटि
articles.summary:
झापा । झापाको मेचीनगरस्थित दिपज्योती टोलका ४२ परिवार दुई दशकअघि किस्ताबन्दीमा खरिद गरेको जग्गाको लालपूर्जा नपाउँदा समस्यामा परेका छन् । मेचीनगर २ र ३ को सिमानास्थित जग्गा हालसम्म नामसारी हुन नसक्दा पीडित परिवारको समस्या झन् जटिल बन्दै गएको छ ।

झापाको मेचीनगर ३ स्थित बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहेको चिया बगान नभएको खाली जग्गा वि.स २०६३÷०६४ सालमा शुभ चिया प्रालिले बैना गरि घरघडेरीका लागि स्थानीयलाई किस्ताबन्दी एकदेखि पाँच कठ्ठासम्म बिक्री प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढायो ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारलाई लक्षित गरी बिक्री गरिएको उक्त जग्गाको अधिकांश किस्ता तिरे पनि अन्तिम किस्ता लिएपछि लालपूर्जा उपलब्ध गराउने सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभएको पीडितहरूको भनाइ छ ।

अन्तिम किस्ता पनि तिर्न तयार भएका उनीहरुको संस्थाले रकम नै लिएन । अहिले उनीहरुको न पैसा फिर्ता भएको छ, न लालपूर्जा नै पाएका छन् ।

त्यस्तै पीडित स्थानीयका अनुसार जग्गा बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहे पनि तत्कालीन शुभ चिया प्रालिका अध्यक्ष हेमराज भारतीले कारोबार अगाडी बढाएका थिए । तर उनले पैसा लिएपछि त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न आलटाल गरेको दुखेसो पीडित पोख्छन् । उनीहरुले जग्गा समस्या तत्काल समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित निकायसँग माग गरेका छन्।

यता शुभ चिया प्रालिका वर्तमान अध्यक्ष रमेश दाहालले विगतमा कारोबार संस्थागत प्रक्रियाअनुसार नभएकाले समस्या उत्पन्न भएको बताउँछन् । समस्या समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायसँग आवश्यक गृहकार्य भइरहेको र पीडितलाई न्याय दिलाउने प्रयास जारी रहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारले साहुसंग ऋण गरेर किस्ता वापतको रकम समेत दिइ सकेको अवस्थामा अन्तिम किस्ता नलिई जग्गाको स्वामित्व समेत प्रदान नगर्दा ४२ परिवार समस्यामा परेका छन् । तसर्थ उनीहरुलाई सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायले यथाशिघ्र समस्या समाधान गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यक देखिन्छ ।

articles.title: नेपाल लाइफको ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान, १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा आर्जन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालको सर्वाधिक विश्वासिलो जीवन बीमा कम्पनीका रूपमा स्थापित नेपाल लाइफ इन्स्योरेन्सले आफ्नो २५ वर्षको गौरवमय यात्रा (सिल्भर जुबिली) का अवसरमा रु. १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा शुल्क (FPI) आर्जन गर्दै जीवन बीमा इतिहासमा नयाँ ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान कायम गरेको छ।

गत आर्थिक वर्षमा रु. १० अर्ब प्रथम बीमा शुल्क आर्जन गरेको कम्पनीले यस वर्ष उक्त उपलब्धिलाई अझ उचाइमा पुर्‍याउँदै बीमा उद्योगमा नयाँ मानक स्थापित गरेको हो।

यस ऐतिहासिक सफलताका अवसरमा कम्पनीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रमण पराजुलीले सम्पूर्ण बीमित, अभिकर्ता, कर्मचारी, शेयरधनी तथा सरोकारवालाहरू प्रति आभार व्यक्त गर्दै आगामी दिनमा अझ थप प्रविधिमैत्री सेवा, नवीन बीमा योजना र उत्कृष्ट सेवा प्रदान गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे ।

articles.title: सिद्धार्थ बैंकद्वारा ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सुविधा सञ्चालनमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सिद्धार्थ बैंक लिमिटेडले ग्राहकहरुको तत्कालको वित्तीय आवश्यकतालाई सहज र सर्वसुलभ बनाउने उद्देश्यका साथ नयाँ कर्जा योजना ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सार्वजनिक गरेको छ।

यस योजना अन्तर्गत ग्राहकहरुले आफ्नो सुन तथा सुनका गरगहनाहरु धितो राखी बैंकबाट अधिकतम रु. ५० लाखसम्मको कर्जा रकम प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्, जसमा धितो सुनको मूल्यांकनका आधारमा बढीमा ७५ प्रतिशतसम्म कर्जा प्रवाह गरिनेछ।

ग्राहकहरूले आफ्नो व्यक्तिगत तथा व्यावसायिक आवश्यकता सहज रूपमा पूरा गर्न सकुन् भन्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको यो सुरक्षित र भरपर्दो सुविधा हालका लागि बैंकको काठमाडौंस्थित न्यूरोड गेट शाखाबाट उपलब्ध छ, र यस सम्बन्धी थप जानकारीका लागि बैंकको २४ सै घण्टा सञ्चालनमा रहने ग्राहक सेवा केन्द्र ‘सिद्धार्थ केयर’ मा सम्पर्क गर्न सकिनेछ।

articles.title: कतारमा नेपाली समुदायद्वारा स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली
articles.summary:
कतार । गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) राष्ट्रिय समन्वय परिषद् (एनसीसी) कतारले स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस फादर अमिर शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्न शोकसभा आयोजना गरेको छ।

कार्यक्रममा उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व तथा कतारको समृद्धि, विकास र विश्वमञ्चमा स्थापित गराउन पुर्‍याएको अतुलनीय योगदानको उच्च सम्मान गरिएको थियो।

कार्यक्रममा कतारस्थित नेपाली राजदूतावासका कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेल प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी भएका थिए। साथै कतारमा क्रियाशील विभिन्न नेपाली सामाजिक तथा कल्याणकारी संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेखनीय उपस्थिति रहेको थियो। शोकको यस घडीमा नेपाली समुदायले एकता र ऐक्यबद्धता प्रदर्शन गरेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ।

कार्यक्रमको सुरुआत पवित्र कुरआनको तिलावतबाट भएको थियो भने मौलाना गुलाम नबी रजबीले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको आत्माको चिरशान्तिको कामना गर्दै कतार राज्यको शान्ति, स्थायित्व र समृद्धिका लागि विशेष दुआ गरेका थिए।

एनआरएनए एनसीसी कतारका अध्यक्ष कृष्ण पन्थीले स्वागत मन्तव्य दिँदै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको निधनप्रति गहिरो दुःख व्यक्त गरे।

उनले कतारका अमिर, राजपरिवार, सरकार तथा सम्पूर्ण कतारी जनताप्रति समवेदना व्यक्त गर्दै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व, राष्ट्र निर्माणमा खेलेको ऐतिहासिक भूमिका र उनले छोडेको प्रेरणादायी विरासतको प्रशंसा गरे। पन्थीले कतारलाई विश्वकै सम्मानित र समृद्ध राष्ट्रका रूपमा स्थापित गर्न फादर अमिरको योगदान अविस्मरणीय रहेको बताए।

कार्यक्रमका प्रमुख वक्ता प्राध्यापक मोहम्मद रमजान अली मियाँले नेपाल–कतारबीचको लामो समयदेखिको मित्रवत सम्बन्ध र बढ्दो सहकार्यबारे चर्चा गरे। उनले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको नेतृत्वमा कतारले आर्थिक विविधीकरण, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य, पूर्वाधार विकास तथा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कूटनीतिमा उल्लेखनीय प्रगति हासिल गरेको बताए। साथै कतारले हजारौँ नेपालीलाई रोजगारी तथा अवसर उपलब्ध गराउँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै त्यसप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरे।

कतारस्थित नेपाली दूतावासका तर्फबाट बोल्दै कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेलले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्दै उनको योगदानको उच्च प्रशंसा गरे।

उनले नेपाल–कतारबीचको मैत्रीपूर्ण सम्बन्ध निरन्तर सुदृढ हुँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै आगामी दिनमा दुई देशबीचको सहयोग र मित्रतालाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी विभिन्न नेपाली संघ–संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले पनि शोक मन्तव्य व्यक्त गर्दै कतारले नेपाली समुदायलाई प्रदान गरेको अवसरप्रति आभार प्रकट गरे। साथै कठिन घडीमा कतारका नेतृत्व र जनताप्रति ऐक्यबद्धता तथा सम्मान व्यक्त गरे।

श्रद्धाञ्जली सभा अन्त्यमा स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीको सम्मानमा सामूहिक प्रार्थना तथा एक मिनेट मौनधारण गरिएको थियो। कार्यक्रममा वक्ताहरूले उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व र योगदानले आगामी पुस्तालाई पनि प्रेरणा दिइरहने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका थिए।

articles.title: मिटर ब्याज पीडितलाई मनाउन सुधनको कसरत, बल्ल माने पीडित
articles.summary:
बारा । बाराको निजगढ नगरपालिका–८ स्थित निजगढ नगर उद्योग वाणिज्य संघको सभाहलमा तीन दिनदेखि जारी सरकार र मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलनको निर्णायक वार्ता अब राजधानी काठमाडौंमा हुने भएको छ । मिटरब्याज पीडित सरकारसँग वार्ता गर्न जहाजबाट काठमाडौं आएका छन् ।

जनकपुरबाट काठमाडौंतर्फ पैदल न्याय मार्चमा रहेका मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलन, नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूसँग गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले बुधबार करिब पाँच घण्टा लामो छलफल गरेका थिए । छलफलका क्रममा आन्दोलनकारीहरूले उठाएका छ बुँदे मागबारे विस्तृत रूपमा कुराकानी भएको थियो ।

आन्दोलन पक्षका अनुसार सरकारले उनीहरूले अघि सारेका सम्पूर्ण माग कार्यान्वयन गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको छ । बुधबार राति निष्कर्षविहीन बनेको वार्तापछि नेपाल सरकारका गृहमन्त्री सुदन गुरुङले आन्दोलनकारीलाई वार्ता टोली गठन गरी सिंहदरबारस्थित गृह मन्त्रालयमा आउन आग्रह गरेका थिए ।

वार्ताका क्रममा गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले सहमतिपत्रमा रहेका केही शब्द तथा भाषागत विषयमा संशोधन गर्न आवश्यक रहेको बताएका थिए । कानुनी तथा प्राविधिक पक्षसमेत मिलाउनुपर्ने भएकाले तत्काल हस्ताक्षर गर्नु उपयुक्त नहुने उनको भनाइ थियो ।

त्यसपछि गृहमन्त्रीको पटक–पटकको आग्रह र आन्दोलनकारी पक्षको आन्तरिक छलफलपछि मिटरब्याजविरुद्ध किसान–मजदुर आन्दोलन, नेपालले पाँच सदस्यीय वार्ता टोली गठन गरी बिहीबार काठमाडौं प्रस्थान गरेको हो । अन्य आन्दोलनकारी भने वार्ताको नतिजा नआएसम्म बाराको निजगढमै रहने जनाइएको छ ।

काठमाडौं प्रस्थान आएको पाँच सदस्यीय वार्ता टोलीको संयोजकमा केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष अवधेश कुश्वाहा रहेका छन् । टोलीमा केन्द्रीय महासचिव मनोज कुमार पासवान, केन्द्रीय प्रवक्ता रिजन राना मगर, केन्द्रीय हेडक्वाटर सदस्य लक्ष्मी घिमिरे तथा केन्द्रीय हेडक्वाटर सदस्य किरण परियार सदस्य रहेका छन् । वार्ता टोलीको रोहबरमा संयुक्त जनअधिकार मोर्चाका केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष निर्ग नवीन लगायतका प्रतिनिधिहरू पनि काठमाडौं आएका छन् ।

आन्दोलनका केन्द्रीय अध्यक्ष अवधेश कुश्वाहाले सरकारले माग पूरा गर्न सकारात्मक प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको भए पनि त्यसलाई कानुनी रूपमा स्पष्ट र लिखित रूपमा सुनिश्चित गर्नुपर्ने बताए ।

उनले आन्दोलनकारीको उद्देश्य सहमतिपत्रमा हस्ताक्षर मात्र नभई त्यसको प्रभावकारी कार्यान्वयन सुनिश्चित गर्नु रहेको उल््लेख गर्दै वार्ता सकारात्मक निष्कर्षमा पुग्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: कांग्रेस नेता अभिषेक गिरीको अपराध साम्राज्य !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ‘हिजो गल्ती भयो, अब समाजसेवामा लाग्छु’ भनी करिब तीन वर्षअघि कारागारबाट छुट्दा अभिषेक गिरीले दिएको सन्देशले धेरैलाई उनी बदलिएको विश्वास दिलाएको थियो । तर, समाजसेवाको आवरणमा पुरानै आपराधिक सञ्जाल सञ्चालन गरेको आरोपमा अहिले उनी फेरि प्रहरी नियन्त्रणमा छन् । मोरङ प्रहरी र केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो (सीआईबी) दुवैले उनीविरुद्ध ठगी र आपराधिक विश्वासघातसम्बन्धी उजुरीमाथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेका छन् ।

२०७९ चैत ५ गते नौ वर्ष जेल सजाय भुक्तान गरेर कारागारबाट निस्कँदा अभिषेक गिरी साधु भएको आभाष दिलाएका थिए । विगतका गल्ती नदोहो¥याउने प्रतिवद्धता जनाउँदै उनले समाजसेवामा समर्पित हुने घोषणा गरेका थिए ।

त्यसपछि उनले ‘गिरी फाउन्डेसन’ स्थापना गरे, सामाजिक कार्यक्रममा सक्रिय देखिए र आर्थिक रूपमा विपन्नलाई सहयोग गर्न थाले । तर, प्रहरी अनुसन्धानले अभिषेक समाजसेवाको आडमा आपराधिक क्रियाकलापमा संलग्न रहेको भन्दै गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएको छ ।

गिरीमाथि लागेको आरोप के हो ?

अहिले सीआईबीले अनुसन्धानका लागि मोरङबाट काठमाडौं ल्याएका गिरीलाई यसअघि जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय मोरङले पक्राउ गरेको थियो । उनी पक्राउ परेको विषय पनि निकै रोचक छ । कारागार बाहिरका मान्छेको कारागारभित्र कुनै पहुँच हुँदैन ।

कुनै कैदीबन्दीलाई भेट्न जानु प¥यो भने पनि भेटघाटको कारण खुलाउँदै प्रशासनको अनुमति लिएर सुरक्षा जाँच पार गर्नुपर्ने हुन्छ । अझ कारागारभित्रको प्रशासनको बाहिर कुनै साइनो नै हुँदैन । यति सुरक्षित रहने कारागारको शासन भने गिरीले बाहिरै बसेर चलाउँथे ।

कैदीबन्दीको रासन भत्तामा समेत कब्जा जमाएर असुल्ने गरेको भन्दै गिरीविरुद्ध कैदीबन्दीले नै आवाज उठाएका थिए ।

कैदीबन्दीले बनाएको मुढा र गलैँचाको पैसा गिरीले बुझ्ने गरेको आरोप छ । असार १२ गते कैदीबन्दीलाई बाँडेको १३ लाख ४० हजार रुपैयाँ असुल गरेको आरोप पनि गिरीमाथि छ ।

कारागारभित्रको खाद्यान्न र तरकारी आपूर्तिमा समेत उनको सिन्डिकेट चल्ने गरेको कैदीबन्दीको गुनासो थियो । प्रहरीका अनुसार, गिरीमाथि अहिले दुई फरक प्रकृतिका आरोपमा अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ ।

मोरङमा कारागारभित्र हुने आर्थिक गतिविधिमा बाहिरबाट प्रभाव पार्दै कैदीबन्दीको रासन भत्ता, उनीहरूले उत्पादन गरेका सामग्रीको रकम तथा आपूर्ति व्यवस्थामा अवैध हस्तक्षेप गरेको आरोपका आधारमा असार १३ गते मोरङ प्रहरीले उनलाई पक्राउ गरेको हो । उनको घरमा गरिएको खानतलासीका क्रममा नगद गन्ने मेसिनसमेत फेला परेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ ।

उच्च अदालत विराटनगरको आदेशपछि उनी मोरङबाट छुटे पनि त्यही दिन सीआईबीले पुनः नियन्त्रणमा लियो । यसपटक भने निर्माण व्यवसायी सुवास श्रेष्ठको उजुरीका आधारमा अनुसन्धान अघि बढाइएको छ ।

पहुँचका आधारमा ठेक्का दिलाइदिने आश्वासन दिएर ठगी गरेको, निर्माण उपकरण नियन्त्रणमा लिएको तथा जबर्जस्ती सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण गराएको आरोपमा आपराधिक विश्वासघात र ठगीसम्बन्धी अनुसन्धान भइरहेको सीआईबीको भनाइ छ । प्रहरीले घटनासँग सम्बन्धित प्रमाण संकलन र बयान लिने काम जारी रहेको जनाएको छ ।

अभिषेक गिरीको आपराधिक पृष्ठभूमि

अभिषेक गिरीको आपराधिक पृष्ठभूमि भने लामो छ । प्रहरीको अभिलेखअनुसार उनी पहिलो पटक २०५८ सालमा पक्राउ परेका थिए । त्यसयता कुटपिट, सार्वजनिक अपराध, डाँका चोरी, ज्यान मार्ने उद्योग र अन्ततः अपहरण तथा शरीर बन्धकजस्ता विभिन्न मुद्दामा उनी ११ पटकसम्म पक्राउ परिसकेका छन् ।

२०७१ सालमा अपहरण तथा शरीर बन्धक मुद्दामा दोषी ठहर भएपछि उनले लामो जेल सजाय भुक्तान गरेका थिए । कारागारबाट छुटेपछि उनी सामाजिक र राजनीतिक गतिविधिमा समेत सक्रिय बने । तर, पछिल्ला घटनाक्रमले उनको पुनः आपराधिक गतिविधिसँग सम्बन्ध रहेको आरोपलाई प्रहरीले गम्भीर रूपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

अनुसन्धान अझै जारी रहेकाले उनीमाथि लागेको आरोप अदालतबाट प्रमाणित भइसकेको अवस्था भने होइन । अब प्रहरी अनुसन्धान र अदालतको अन्तिम निर्णयले अभिषेक गिरीको कर्तुतको नयाँ पर्दाफास हुनेछ ।

articles.title: अपरेसन चार्लीबाट खुलेको रहस्य, नक्कली नोट छाप्ने गिरोह पक्राउ
articles.summary:
रुपन्देही । रुपन्देही प्रहरीले नक्कली नेपाली नोट, नोट छाप्न प्रयोग गरिएका उपकरण र त्यसमा संलग्न मानिसहरुलाई पक्राउ गरी सार्वजनिक गरेको छ । जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय भैरहवामा बुधबार पत्रकार सम्मेलन गरी प्रहरीले उक्त कार्यमा संलग्नहरु बारे जानकारी दिएको हो ।

रुपन्देही प्रहरीले नक्कली नोट, छाप्ने मेसिनरी उपकरणसहित ६ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको छ । असार २६ गते बुटवलमा चिनजानकै गंगा कुमारी पुर्वछानेले एक महिलालाई इसेवामार्फत् २ हजार १ सय रुपैयाँ ट्रान्सफर गर्न लगाएर दुईवटा हजारका नोट दिएकी थिइन् ।

पछि ती नोट नक्कली भएको थाहा पाएपछि पीडित महिलाले इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय बुटवलमा निवेदन दिएकी थिइन् । पूर्वछानेलाई नियन्त्रणमा लिएर अनुसन्धान गर्ने क्रममा नक्कली नोट, छाप्ने मेसिनरी उपकरणसहित प्रहरीले ६ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको हो ।

अनुसन्धानका क्रममा बुटवल र पोखराका आरोपीहरुका घरबाट समेत नक्कली एक हजार दरका नोट प्रहरीले बरामद गरेको छ ।

डीएसपी चन्दका अनुसार पक्राउ पर्नेमा रुपन्देहीको बुटवल

उपमहानगरपालिका–११, सिर्जनानगर बस्ने बर्ष ३६ की गंगा कुमारी पुर्वछाने, कास्कीको पोखरा महानगरपालिका–१ बस्ने कृष्ण भन्ने किरण कृष्ण तिवारी, भक्तपुरको चाँगुनारायण नगरपालिका–१ बस्ने रामचन्द्र खत्री, कपिलवस्तुको बाणगंगा नगरपालालिका–२ बस्ने संजय थारु, दोलखाको सैलुङ गाउँपालिका–४ वस्ने वर्ष ३८ को पासाङ तामाङ र भारत पश्चिम बंगाल सिलुगुढी भक्तिनगर थाना बस्ने वर्ष ४९ को बासुमित्र आनन्द रहेका छन् ।

उनीहरुको घर तथा शरीर खानतलासीको क्रममा तयार भएका सक्कली जस्तो देखिने एक हजार दरका नक्कली नेपाली नोट ६ सय २२ थान बरामद गरिएको डीएसपी चन्दले बताए ।

प्रहरी फोटोकपी मेसिन, डेल कम्पनीको ल्याप्टप, नक्कली नोट कटिङ गर्न प्रयोग हुने मेसिन, नक्कली नोट प्रिन्ट गर्न प्रयोग हुने प्रिन्टर, नक्कली नोट छाप्न प्रयोग गर्ने पेपर १ कार्टुन पनि बरामद गरेको छ ।

यस्तै, नक्कली नोट बनाउन प्रयोग हुने केमिकल, लेमिलेसन मेसिन, प्लाष्टिक पेपर र ६ वटा मोबाइल पनि प्रहरीले बरामद गरेको छ ।

पीडित महिलाको निवेदनका आधारमा लुम्बिनी प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालय दाङ, जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय र इलका प्रहरी कार्यालय बुटवलले ‘अपरेसन चार्ली’ नाम दिएर नक्कली नोट सम्बन्धी संयुक्त अनुसन्धान सुरु गरेका थिए ।

पक्राउ गरेमा ६ जनाविरुद्ध रुपन्देही जिल्ला अदालतबाट मुद्रा सम्बन्धी कसूरमा ५ दिनको म्याद थप गरी अनुसन्धान जारी राखिएको प्रहरीे जनाएको छ । रुपन्देहीमा यसअघि पनि लुम्बिनी, सालझण्डी र बुटवलमै नक्कली नोट बरामद भएका थिए ।

articles.title: Chinese envoy voices concerns over upcoming Tibetan studies seminar in Kathmandu
articles.summary:
Chinese Ambassador to Nepal Zhang Maoming has expressed concerns over the upcoming 17th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies to be organised from August 23-29 in Kathmandu.

Ambassador Zhang met Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai on Tuesday and discussed the upcoming event, said one senior foreign ministry official. The Chinese envoy drew the attention of the foreign secretary and cautioned that the event could be used by supporters of the exiled Tibetan spiritual leader Dalai Lama, according to the official.

The envoy said some individuals could speak against China and in support of Tibet, and urged officials to make sure that no such things happen, the official told the Post.

Hundreds of researchers, scholars and experts on Tibetan studies from around the globe will gather at the event.

According to the website of the International Association of Tibetan Studies, the seminar will be organised jointly by the Himalaya Centre for Asian Studies, Kathmandu University (HiCAS, KU); and the Kathmandu University Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute (KU-CBS at RYI). The conveners are Prof Sagar Sharma (HiCAS) and Prof Thomas Doctor (KU-CBS at RYI).

Some Kathmandu-based individuals sympathetic to Beijing’s position on Tibet have also expressed concern over the event saying that promoting Tibetan language, culture and history could ultimately be interpreted as support for the Dalai Lama's views.

“Recently the government allowed Tibetan refugees to celebrate the birthday of the Dalai Lama and now this event is happening,” said one observer who has been following the Tibetan matter in Nepal. “That is why the Chinese side expressed reservations over the upcoming event.”

The Chinese ambassador, however, did not submit any written reservation or called for cancellation of the event, but voiced his concerns, the foreign ministry official told the Post.

Those who registered for the conference had to pay $360 for early registration and $440 for late registration, the Post has learnt. Registration for the event closed on June 15.

One official at the Chinese Embassy confirmed that Ambassador Zhang met with foreign secretary Rai but asked the Post to seek comment from the foreign ministry.

As per the itinerary, the opening Ceremony will be held at Kathmandu University’s Dhulikhel campus, and the rest of the programmes will be held at Hotel Soaltee.

The board members of the International Association for Tibetan Studies are Daniel Berounský (Czech Republic), Geshe Nyima Woser Choekhortshang Rinpoche (Nepal), Hildegard Diemberger (Austria), Dorji Wangchuk (Bhutan), Iwao Kazushi (Japan). Lama Jabb (UK), Pema Choedon (Norway), Karma Phuntsho (Bhutan), Françoise Pommaret (France), Jarmila Ptáčková (Czech Republic), Françoise Robin (France)., Ulrike Roesler (UK) and Yudru Tsomu (China).

Formally established in 1979 at the University of Oxford, it operates as a non-political academic body dedicated to advancing research in Tibetan history, religion, linguistics, and art.

Prof Sharma of Kathmandu University said that scholars and professors from world-renowned universities like Oxford and Cambridge will attend the conference. Scholars from 39 countries who are experts in the field of Tibetan Studies will participate.

“Its not a pro-Dalai Lama event. Huge numbers of Chinese professors and scholars are also attending. The Chinese embassy also knows about it. We have also informed different government agencies,” said Sharma.

articles.title: Lawmakers seek government control of hotel room rates. Hoteliers call it regressive
articles.summary:
Lawmakers have proposed allowing the government to regulate the room rates charged by star and other classified hotels under amendments to Nepal’s proposed Integrated Tourism Bill. Hoteliers have criticised the proposal saying it would distort the market and that room rates should be left to market.

The bill is currently undergoing clause-by-clause scrutiny at a parliamentary committee after 58 lawmakers registered 263 amendments before its final debate and vote in parliament.

Lawmakers Shishir Khadka and Nitima Bhandari Karki have proposed a new provision barring any individual or institution from charging rates above those prescribed by the government.

Under the proposal, star hotels and all classified hotels would be required to charge only within a government-approved pricing structure based on their official classification and service quality.

The proposal comes as Nepal’s hotel industry struggles with excess capacity and intense price competition. The country now has more than 1,600 hotels offering around 64,000 room nights, including 222 star-rated properties. While hotel supply has expanded rapidly, tourist arrivals have failed to keep pace, leading to widespread undercutting.

According to government data, foreign tourists stayed in Nepal for a record average of 16.34 days in 2025. However, their average daily spending dropped to $33.09, the second-lowest level on record and well below the regional average of $100 to $150. Industry insiders partly attribute the decline to aggressive discounting by hotels.

Hoteliers, however, argue that government intervention in pricing would be counterproductive.

“Hotel rates are determined by the services they provide, not simply by their star classification,” said Sahadev Dhamala, managing director of Kathmandu Eco Hotel and a newly appointed board member of the Nepal Tourism Board.

He said many boutique hotels and small resorts charge higher rates than some five-star hotels because of their unique products and services.

“Room rates automatically adjust to travel trends, the local economy and different market segments such as corporate and leisure travellers,” Dhamala said. “Capping rates would be counterproductive.”

Industry leaders say hotels worldwide use dynamic pricing, adjusting room rates in real time in response to demand, supply, competitors’ prices and seasonal trends.

Binayak Shah, president of the Hotel Association Nepal, described the proposal as a regressive step.

“Hotels operate entirely on the principles of demand and supply,” Shah said. “The private sector has invested billions of rupees in hospitality. Instead of capping room rates, the government should focus on bringing more tourists to Nepal.”

The proposal follows a similar experiment in Sri Lanka, which imposed minimum room rates for Colombo city five-star hotels at $100 in October 2023. The policy was challenged in court by sections of the tourism industry, which argued it had been introduced without adequate consultation and discouraged convention and business travellers by making hotel stays more expensive than competing regional destinations. In May 2024, Sri Lanka’s Court of Appeal suspended the mandatory pricing system, and restored market-based pricing.

The amendments also seek to tighten regulations governing the use of star classifications.

Lawmakers have proposed prohibiting any hotel from advertising, promoting or marketing itself as a “star hotel” unless it fully meets government-prescribed standards. Hotels falsely claiming star status would face legal action.

Current regulations classify hotels primarily by room capacity and service standards. Within Kathmandu Valley, a five-star deluxe hotel must have at least 150 rooms, while a standard five-star hotel requires 100 rooms. Outside the Valley, the minimum requirements are 100 and 80 rooms respectively, along with standards covering room size, facilities and service quality.

Several lawmakers have also proposed expanding the bill’s focus beyond hotel regulation.

Lawmaker Ganga Laxmi Awal has proposed making traditional Newari architecture mandatory for hotels and homestays located in designated heritage areas instead of modern concrete designs.

Another amendment, proposed by lawmaker Sumnima Udas, seeks to promote sustainable, green and climate-resilient tourism. It calls for tourism infrastructure to prioritise environmental conservation, carbon emission reduction, waste management and renewable energy use, while encouraging climate adaptation measures in Himalayan and other environmentally sensitive areas. It also proposes incentives for tourism enterprises to obtain green certification.

The bill also includes provisions to ensure tourism benefits reach local communities by promoting community-based tourism, homestays and the use of local products. It further proposes training, awareness programmes and preferential support to help communities historically excluded from tourism because of ethnic, gender or social discrimination participate in the sector. The bill also encourages businesses to employ local workers and source locally produced goods and services.

articles.title: Government collects billions from students despite free education laws
articles.summary:
Despite the constitutional guarantee of free education up to the secondary level, the government continues to charge students thousands of rupees in mandatory fees under various headings, generating more than Rs2.5 billion in annual revenue from students alone.

Article 31 of the constitution guarantees every citizen the right to free and compulsory education up to the basic level (grade 8) and free education up to the secondary level (grade 12). To enforce this provision, Parliament enacted the Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education in 2018, followed by the Compulsory and Free Education Regulations in 2020.

Yet students and their parents must bear more than a dozen government-imposed charges throughout secondary school. The continued collection of these fees has raised questions over whether the state has fulfilled its promise of free education up to grade 12.

A student pays more than Rs5,000 to the government in various mandatory charges between grades 9 and 12. Every year, between 400,000 and 600,000 students enrol in those grades. Based on enrolment figures, the government collects more than Rs2.5 billion annually through registration, examination and academic certificate fees alone. It also continues to levy numerous additional charges that critics say are incompatible with the constitutional guarantee of free education.

According to the National Examinations Board, every student enrolled in both community and private schools must pay a registration fee of Rs300 upon joining grade 9.

When they reach grade 10, schools collect an examination application fee of Rs500 from each student and deposit it with the government. Narayan Pokhrel, information officer at the Board, said students must also pay Rs400 for subject registration in grade 11. Around 400,000 students enrol in grade 11 every year.

After paying fees in grades 9, 10 and 11, students are required to pay another Rs800 examination application fee in grade 12. Even after passing the examinations, they must pay additional charges to obtain their academic certificates for both grade 10 and grade 12.

While the Ministry of Education and Sports has not prohibited subordinate agencies from charging students, the Board and the Office of the Controller of Examinations continue to collect these fees, including from students attending community schools, where education is supposed to be free.

“The government itself instructs schools to collect registration, subject registration, examination application and certificate fees from students and deposit the money with the authorities,” the principal of a community school in Kathmandu told Kantipur.

Long queues of students can be seen every day at the Board's central and provincial offices to obtain academic certificates or correct errors in them. In many cases, schools collect the fees directly from students before forwarding them to the Board.

Sneha Rupakheti, who passed grade 12 this year, said she paid Rs1,500 to receive her transcript, migration certificate and provisional certificate. She said she had already paid another Rs2,000 in registration, examination application and subject registration fees between grades 9 and 12.

She also spent Rs1,500 to obtain her grade 10 certificate.

Parents have complained that some schools charge students more than the government-prescribed fees and retain part of the additional amount for their own expenses. Students and parents also allege that private schools routinely collect more than the fees fixed by the board.

According to information provided by the board, students in grades 11 and 12 are subject to fees under 20 different categories.

Students must pay Rs500 for a supplementary certificate and Rs500 each for duplicate copies of academic certificates. A permanent certificate costs an additional Rs1,000. The board charges Rs500 to authenticate an original certificate and another Rs500 to verify copies of mark sheets, grade sheets and certificates.

Students dissatisfied with their examination results must pay Rs1,000 to apply for re-totalling, which is verification of total marks awarded on an answer sheet. This year, around 32,000 grade 12 students submitted online applications for re-totalling after paying the fee.

Even when mistakes are made by board officials, examiners or teachers, students must pay to have their results reviewed. In this year's Secondary Education Examination (SEE), around 34,000 students applied for re-totalling, and the results of more than 1,800 were revised after errors were found.

Students who remain dissatisfied after re-totalling must pay Rs1,500 to view their grade 12 answer sheets. If they then seek a full re-evaluation, they must pay another Rs2,000.

The board also charges Rs500 to correct errors in names or dates of birth on certificates, Rs500 to trace a symbol number and Rs50 for a duplicate payment receipt, according to Pokhrel.

Students in grade 9 and 10 are also subjected to more than a dozen different government-imposed fees.

For grade 10, students must pay Rs500 each for a grade sheet, original certificate, migration certificate, verification of original certificate, verification of duplicate certificate and duplicate copy of lost certificate. Officials said these fees are deposited directly into the government's revenue account.

Students seeking to consolidate academic certificates must pay another Rs500.

The fees for re-totalling, viewing answer-sheets and re-evaluation differ between the SEE and grade 12 examinations. For the SEE, students must pay Rs500 per subject for re-totalling, while answer-sheet viewing and re-evaluation cost Rs2,000 each.

The Office of the Controller of Examinations also charges between Rs250 and Rs500 to correct names, surnames and dates of birth, including English-language dates of birth, on SEE certificates.

The National Examinations Board defends the charges, stating that they are essential to keep the examination system running.

Janga Bahadur Aryal, member secretary of the board, said the fees have long been collected as per decisions made by the board.

“The money collected from grade 11 and 12 students is deposited directly into the board's account. It is used to run the board's offices, manage staff, conduct examinations, publish results and carry out all of our operations. The government does not provide us with a separate budget,” Aryal said. “The money collected from students in grades 9 and 10, however, is deposited into the government's revenue account.”

The government collects around Rs180 million annually from grade 9 registration fees alone. It raises another Rs250 million from the same students through grade 10 examination application fees.

Officials at the Office of the Controller of Examinations said it collects around Rs600 million in revenue each year. Of that amount, roughly Rs350 million is generated from the Secondary Education Examination, while the remaining revenue is deposited into the Ministry of Finance's revenue account.

Yet the Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education explicitly prohibits such charges.

The law states that providing education up to the secondary level is the responsibility of the state. Section 4 of the Act provides that “the responsibility for providing education up to the secondary level shall rest with the State.”

The Compulsory and Free Education Regulations also stipulate that no fees should be charged.

Former education minister Bidya Bhattarai said she had tried to end the practice while in office.

In January 2025, Bhattarai secured a decision prohibiting the collection of fees from students. The proposal was endorsed by the National Development Problem Solving Committee, chaired by the prime minister, and forwarded to the Ministry of Finance. However, it was never implemented.

“On the one hand, the law guarantees free education. On the other hand, state agencies themselves continue to collect fees,” Bhattarai said.

“At the time, we agreed that registration fees for grades 9 and 11 should be scrapped immediately, while decisions on examination and certificate fees would be taken gradually,” she said. “But I was removed as education minister before the decision could be implemented.”

She said the ministry had proposed that students should register only once during secondary education and that the registration should be free.

“It is contradictory for the government to tell local governments and schools not to charge students in the name of free education while the federal government itself continues to collect money from them,” Bhattarai said.

She added that her ministry had also prepared a roadmap for implementing the Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education.

The Office of the Auditor General has repeatedly questioned the legality of the fees.

In its 2024 annual report, the constitutional watchdog noted that despite constitutional and legal provisions guaranteeing free education up to the secondary level, the National Examinations Board continues to collect registration, examination and certificate fees from secondary school students.

Nepal has 27,010 community schools and 8,941 private schools. According to the Ministry of Education, around 5.2 million students study in community schools, and another 3 million attend private schools. The ministry said students in both public and private schools are required to pay these government-imposed fees.

Shiva Kumar Sapkota, joint secretary and spokesperson for the Ministry of Education, acknowledged that the government's fee structure should be revised to bring it into line with the Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education.

“The ministry has been working to remove the provisions that allow these fees to be charged,” Sapkota said. “However, because these fees are also a source of government revenue, the issue does not fall under the Ministry of Education alone.”

He argued that the fees collected by the Board are determined under its authority as an autonomous institution.

Education expert Binay Kumar Kushiyait said successive governments have failed to implement the Act Relating to Compulsory and Free Education.

“Under the constitution, no one should be charging students any fee up to grade 12,” he said. “Successive governments have failed. No government has shown the commitment, accountability or responsibility needed to ensure genuinely free education.”

Kushiyait said the government continues to rely on student fees because it has failed to allocate sufficient funding to the education sector.

He also pointed out that many community schools are forced to charge students and parents simply to cover operating expenses.

“Community schools serve the poorest children, Dalits, students from remote and marginalised communities, and children with disabilities,” he said. “Instead of charging them, the state should make every aspect of their education free and provide scholarships to encourage them to stay in school.”

articles.title: Skyrocketing fuel costs drive sharp decline in Nepali air travel
articles.summary:
Costly jet fuel in Nepal has forced domestic carriers to hike airfares by up to 40 percent, causing passenger numbers to plunge.

Escalating geopolitical tensions—driven by joint US and Israeli military operations in Iran—have sent global aviation fuel prices skyrocketing.

According to data compiled by domestic airlines and Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN), the number of domestic passengers plunged by over 540,000 in the fiscal year 2025-26, which ended on July 16, mainly due to fuel price hike.

The data shows that total internal passenger traffic dropped 12 percent compared to the fiscal year 2024-25. Numbers fell from 4,557,634 passengers in the 2024-25 fiscal year to 4,016,880 in 2025-26—a net loss of 540,754 travellers.

The slump was particularly severe during the final five months of the fiscal year, from February to July. Monthly figures show passenger volume shrank by 10 percent in the Nepali month of Falgun (mid-February to mid-March), 17 percent in mid-March to mid-April, 33 percent in mid-April to mid-May, 34 percent in mid-May to mid-June, and 29 percent in mid-June to mid-July.

“The direct shock of the international energy crisis hit our domestic sector squarely during this period,” said Yubaraj Bista, chief business officer at Yeti Airlines. “While flight numbers in the first six months remained steady, the sudden spike in fuel costs made air travel unaffordable for ordinary citizens and domestic tourists.”

The downturn hit all major domestic carriers, including Buddha Air, Yeti Airlines, and Shree Airlines. Buddha Air experienced the largest numerical loss, dropping 394,000 passengers—a 14 percent decline that accounted for nearly 73 percent of the industry’s total drop.

Despite the contraction, Buddha Air maintained its market lead with a 58.3 percent share. Yeti Airlines lost 93,048 passengers (a 9 percent decline), holding a 22.5 percent market share, while Shree Airlines proved relatively resilient with a modest 6 percent drop.

Industry leaders warn that the financial strain threatens carrier solvency. Pratap Jung Pandey, president of the Airlines Operators Association of Nepal (AOAN) and operator of Kailash Helicopter, described the situation as critical.

“This is the second major crisis facing Nepali aviation since the Covid-19 pandemic,” said Pandey. “Balance sheets across several airlines have turned negative, and many operators are finding it difficult simply to survive.”

According to Pandey, operational costs have escalated further due to currency depreciation. “Fuel prices remain high and volatile,” he said. “Crucially, fees paid by airlines to CAAN are denominated in US dollars, as are spare parts, yet our income is entirely in Nepali rupees.”

The helicopter sector has felt a similar pinch, with flight hours down 20 to 30 percent across Nepal’s 11 helicopter operators.

The passenger decline spanned nearly every major airport in Nepal. Simara experienced the steepest drop at 24 percent, followed by Bhairahawa at 22 percent. Traffic at Pokhara shrank by 11 percent, while Nepalgunj fell by 16 percent. Dhangadhi dropped 13 percent, Surkhet 15 percent, and Rajbiraj 10 percent. Biratnagar and Bhadrapur each saw 7 percent decreases, while Janakpur recorded a 6 percent decline.

Nepal’s domestic aviation market relies on roughly 4 to 4.5 million passengers annually. Around 300,000 are foreign tourists, 300,000 Indian visitors, and 100,000 employees of Nepal government and non-governmental organisations. The remaining 3.9 million journeys are made by ordinary Nepalis travelling once or twice a year for family visits, medical treatment, or social obligations.

“When airfares rose, these occasional domestic travellers simply chose not to fly,” Bista explained. “Additionally, following recent political changes, daily market tracking shows a noticeable reduction in political leaders and cadres travelling to and from Kathmandu.”

Domestic airlines in Nepal faced compounding challenges over the past year, including rising insurance premiums and stringent regulatory safety audits. The added burden of fuel price volatility has further squeezed operational margins across the board.

In response to the crisis, airline representatives recently met with CAAN Director General Mukesh Dangol to seek government intervention. The AOAN representatives pointed out that while CAAN and the International Civil Aviation Organisation closely monitor technical safety, no state mechanism addresses the financial viability of domestic airlines, leaving operators exposed during external economic shocks.

articles.title: Left alliance can only succeed with a clear purpose
articles.summary:
There is nothing new about Nepali political parties, particularly the communist forces, forming alliances and merging. Adding a new episode to this recurring trend, the KP Sharma Oli-led CPN-UML and Pushpa Kamal Dahal’s Nepali Communist Party are in intense discussions about forming an alliance, with the larger goal of merging the two parties. If Dahal’s statement in Janakpur is to be believed, a conducive environment for this merger has already been created. He has asked provincial leaders to collaborate with the UML to form governments. Leaders from both parties have realised the need to come together for the national interest.

However, it is clear that the renewed push for an alliance is largely the result of the debacle in the March elections and the need to prepare for the forthcoming provincial and local elections. Both parties suffered a historic defeat in the polls. Barring Nepal’s first general election in 1959, never have the communist parties been reduced to such a weak position.

Nepal has a large number of registered political parties—135 in total—which is quite high for a country with less than 30 million people. Except for the recent election that reduced the number of parties in the House of Representatives to six, Nepal’s Parliament has often had a large number of parties—sometimes dozens. So, an alliance among parties with a common ideology is a welcome development, provided it is long-lasting. More importantly, it should do more good to society than harm. Political stability and policy continuity are possible only when parties come together with a clear purpose that goes beyond electoral calculations and short-term power sharing.

However, past experience shows that such alliances or mergers have done more harm than good to the state machinery. The UML and then CPN (Maoist Centre) jointly contested the 2017 elections before merging in May 2018 to form the Nepal Communist Party. After securing a thumping majority in the parliamentary elections, people expected the unified party to ensure a stable government capable of delivering on its promises. Instead, the party became more engaged in internal disputes than in governance. The prolonged tussle resulted in Oli dissolving the House of Representatives twice, pushing the country into a political crisis. The huge public mandate went to waste.

Now, as they once again move closer, the leadership of both parties should be clear about what the alliance is meant to achieve. This is the right opportunity for them to establish a stable, consolidated party representing communities inclined towards left politics. But if their sole purpose is to form provincial governments or improve their electoral results, they are seriously mistaken. Recent elections have shown that people are increasingly able to distinguish lofty promises from actual delivery and to judge parties by how closely they remain connected to their voters.

Therefore, the two parties face a daunting task in convincing the public that the present attempt at left unity is different from the last one. If they keep repeating past mistakes, no matter what initiative they take, it will not stop further erosion of their political strength or restore the trust they are steadily losing.

articles.title: Inherited political vocabulary meets Nepal’s constitutional reality
articles.summary:
The widespread use of the phrase ‘the Balen Government’ is neither surprising nor inherently incorrect. Political language often favours brevity over constitutional precision, and journalists naturally seek expressions that immediately identify the political leadership of the day. In parliamentary democracies across the Commonwealth, ‘government’ has long served as convenient shorthand for the ministry led by the prime minister and the political party or coalition commanding a legislative majority. The expression therefore carries a long linguistic tradition that is both familiar and easily understood.

Yet constitutional language and political shorthand do not always coincide. While everyday conversation permits broad simplifications, constitutional analysis requires greater precision because terms like this shape how citizens understand the distribution of public authority. The question is therefore not whether people understand what journalists mean by ‘the Balen Government.’ They undoubtedly do. The more interesting question is whether that phrase accurately reflects the constitutional architecture established by Nepal’s 2015 Constitution.

Nepal undoubtedly operates under a parliamentary system in which executive authority is exercised through the Council of Ministers headed by the prime minister. In this respect, it shares important institutional characteristics with Westminster democracies. However, Nepal’s constitutional framework differs from the traditional Westminster model in several significant respects. Unlike the uncodified constitutional tradition of the United Kingdom, Nepal’s constitutional order is defined by an extensive written constitution that carefully distributes authority among numerous constitutional institutions while simultaneously establishing a robust federal structure. Executive authority therefore exists within an elaborate network of constitutional constraints rather than as the singular embodiment of ‘the government.’

This distinction becomes particularly important because Nepal’s Constitution, adopted in the contemporary context, does not simply establish a parliamentary executive. It also creates multiple institutions whose authority neither derives from nor is subordinate to the Prime Minister. Consequently, describing an entire constitutional order through the name of its current prime minister risks obscuring the carefully balanced institutional design envisioned by the Constitution.

For that reason, the expression ‘the Balen administration’ more accurately captures the constitutional role of the prime minister. It identifies the temporary political executive responsible for directing federal policy without implying authority over institutions that remain constitutionally independent.

The constitutional rationale for this distinction can be understood from two complementary perspectives: The horizontal separation of constitutional authority and the vertical distribution of power within Nepal’s federal system.

Horizontal distribution

The first consideration concerns the horizontal organisation of the Nepali state. Although the prime minister leads the federal executive, the Constitution deliberately disperses state authority among several independent constitutional institutions. Executive power is only one component of a broader constitutional framework, not the entirety of the government of Nepal.

The judiciary offers the clearest illustration. The Supreme Court exercises independent judicial authority and possesses the constitutional responsibility to review executive decisions for their legality and constitutionality. Cabinet decisions therefore remain subject to judicial scrutiny rather than executive discretion.

The federal parliament also performs legislative functions independently of the executive, despite the close political relationship characteristic of parliamentary systems. While governments ordinarily command parliamentary majorities, Parliament nevertheless retains its own constitutional identity, procedural autonomy and oversight responsibilities. Parliamentary committees investigate executive performance, approve legislation, scrutinise budgets and hold ministers accountable.

Perhaps even more illustrative are Nepal’s constitutional commissions. Institutions such as the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority, the Auditor General, the Public Service Commission, the Election Commission and other constitutional bodies were intentionally established to operate independent of day-to-day executive direction. They do not function as departments within the Prime Minister’s Office, nor do they report through ordinary ministerial channels.

Collectively, these institutions demonstrate that the constitutional state extends well beyond the Cabinet. The Prime Minister directs one important branch of government, but he neither controls nor embodies the constitutional system as a whole.

Using the expression ‘the Balen administration’ acknowledges this institutional reality. It clearly identifies the Cabinet, ministries and federal civil service responsible for implementing executive policy while avoiding the unintended implication that independent constitutional institutions somehow operate under the prime minister’s authority.

Vertical distribution of federal power

An equally compelling reason for greater semantic precision lies in Nepal’s federal system. The Constitution fundamentally transformed Nepal from a unitary state into a federal democratic republic composed of three constitutionally recognised levels of government: The federal, provincial and local. This transformation represented more than administrative decentralisation. It constitutionally redistributed public authority across multiple autonomous governments, each possessing its own constitutional responsibilities and democratic legitimacy. Thus, the prime minister leads only one level of this federal structure.

Provincial governments exercise authority within constitutionally assigned jurisdictions through their own elected governments and administrative institutions. Local governments similarly possess constitutionally protected authority over municipal governance, local taxation, service delivery, planning and community development. These powers exist not because the federal government delegates them, but because the Constitution itself grants them.

Balendra Shah’s own political career provides perhaps the most persuasive illustration of this constitutional principle. As mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City, he consistently defended local autonomy against perceived federal encroachment. His administration repeatedly emphasised that municipalities are constitutional governments rather than subordinate administrative offices of Singha Durbar. Many of his public disagreements with federal authorities centred precisely on protecting local constitutional jurisdiction.

Now, as prime minister, the same constitutional logic applies in reverse. Just as the federal government was expected to respect Kathmandu’s constitutional autonomy during his mayoralty, today’s federal executive must similarly respect the constitutional independence of provincial and local governments across Nepal. The constitutional boundary has not changed simply because its occupant has.

This continuity illustrates one of federalism’s greatest strengths: Constitutional authority belongs to institutions rather than individuals. Political leadership changes through elections, but constitutional jurisdictions remain constant. Recognising this distinction reinforces the argument for referring to the current executive as the Balen administration rather than the Balen government. The former accurately identifies the federal executive under Prime Minister Shah’s leadership, whereas the latter may unintentionally suggest authority extending across Nepal’s entire multi-level constitutional system.

Language, constitutional literacy and democratic culture

None of this implies that journalists, commentators or ordinary citizens should abandon familiar political vocabulary. Language naturally evolves through convention, and ‘government’ will almost certainly remain common shorthand for the executive.

Nevertheless, constitutional democracies benefit from linguistic precision, particularly during periods of institutional development. Nepal’s federal republic remains relatively young, and public understanding of constitutional boundaries continues to evolve. The words routinely employed by political leaders, journalists, scholars and commentators gradually influence how citizens conceptualise public authority.

If executive leadership is consistently described as synonymous with ‘the government,’ citizens may gradually come to view independent constitutional institutions as subordinate extensions of the prime minister’s office rather than as co-equal components of a shared constitutional order. Similarly, provincial and local governments may increasingly be perceived as administrative branches of the federal executive instead of constitutionally autonomous governments possessing their own democratic legitimacy.

Such perceptions matter because constitutional democracy depends not only upon legal rules but also upon constitutional culture. Respect for institutional autonomy begins with recognising the distinct constitutional roles assigned to different organs of the state.

articles.title: ‘Medicaid fraud’ must not be used to scapegoat resettled Nepali-speaking Bhutanese
articles.summary:
Recent allegations of Medicaid fraud in Ohio, United States, involving some individuals and entities linked to the resettled Bhutanese community, have reopened an older debate in Nepal’s public sphere: Who gets to be called Nepali, who is pushed outside that name and who benefits when identity is stretched or narrowed according to convenience. Home to more than 40,000 resettled former Bhutanese refugees, Ohio has become the latest backdrop for a conversation that has surfaced repeatedly over the years.

There is a recognisable pattern in how resettled Bhutanese people of Nepali-speaking backgrounds are treated in Nepal’s public discourse. For years, many have been welcomed into the idea of a global Nepali family when they sing Nepali songs, celebrate Dashain or speak emotionally about Nepal. But when the recent allegations of fraud emerged, this same cultural intimacy suddenly became inconvenient. Then comes the rush to disassociate, draw hard borders and hastily declare, “They are not Nepalis.” A recent commentary by Bhushan Dahal, a renowned Nepali journalist, is one prominent example of this troubling pattern, but it is far from the only one.

The pattern is almost reflexive: The very moment something goes wrong, it has historically been a common trend to blame the Bhutanese community, not because evidence demanded it, but because they could be an easy target given their vulnerabilities. Individual allegations involving specific people become a ‘Bhutanese fraud problem’, as if criminal liability can be transferred onto an entire displaced population.

This blame-shifting is then reinforced by opportunists who quickly trade in identities for selective solidarity. Some have reached for the fake Bhutanese refugee scandal in Nepal as supporting evidence, as though that history confirms a pattern of Bhutanese deception. It does not. That scandal was conceived, organised and shamefully executed by Nepal’s own political elite, including senior officials and a sitting Home Minister, who exploited the Bhutanese refugee label for financial gain. To invoke that scandal as a character reference against the very community whose name was stolen in it is not only logically wrong, but it strongly compounds the injustice. The treatment of the Nepali language and traditions as suspicious instruments of deception is historically insensitive. The Nepali-speaking Bhutanese were forcibly uprooted from their birthplace in the late 1980s and early 1990s for upholding the very language, dress and ancestry that Bhutan’s despotic state treated as threats to national purity. Their language was removed from schools, their public identity was criminalised and their belonging was questioned because they refused to disappear into enforced cultural uniformity.

To imply that these same songs, festivals and cultural gatherings are a calculated camouflage designed to hide criminal behaviour is a cruel inversion of history. In reality, Nepalis from Nepal do not own the Nepali language and culture as exclusive property. The ancestors of the Nepali-speaking Bhutanese migrated to the hills of Bhutan even before modern Nepal took shape within its current political boundaries.

As prominent Nepali journalist, Rajesh Koirala, has observed of the diaspora in New Hampshire, Dashain among resettled Bhutanese is no borrowed national costume. While many immigrant communities from Nepal are increasingly drawn towards modernised, party-centred events, the resettled Bhutanese have fiercely retained traditional worship and ritual observance. This was never a strategy of camouflage; it was a strategy of cultural survival.

Resettled Bhutanese were not Nepali citizens merely because they speak the Nepali language. Nepal generously hosted them as refugees for nearly two decades, opening its borders to over 100,000 people and continues to shelter close to 7,000 individuals in camps across Jhapa and Morang. And unanimously resettled, and even those languishing in the camps, have always been indebted to Nepal for this gesture. On the specific question of citizenship, voting rights and the legal privileges of the Nepali state, Kathmandu has every right to draw the line.

However, there is a fundamental difference between being politically Nepali and being culturally Nepali, and conflating the two is where the discourse goes wrong. A culture, a language and an ancestral memory are lived, inherited and carried irrespective of political constructs. Kathmandu can decide who holds a Nepali passport, but factually, it cannot decide who holds a Nepali identity. By reducing a cultural identity down to a legal passport, such arguments alienate not just the Bhutanese-Nepali community, but, in a way, the entire Nepali diaspora.

Some resettled Bhutanese, particularly those born and raised in refugee camps, have at times described Nepal as ‘their country’ out of emotional attachment and the experience of statelessness. Growing up stateless, belonging nowhere on paper, produces exactly this kind of confusion. It is a reason for compassion, not a pretext for suspicion. As California-based youth Thakur Kharel wrote on Facebook, “Many of us grew up hearing ‘Bhutangey’ used as an insult. We were told we were not Nepali enough in Nepal, not Bhutanese enough in Bhutan, and now even in America, some people still want to decide when we belong.”

Nepali identity, distinct from the legal matter of citizenship and voting rights, is not a political topic. Outside the domain of passports and electoral rolls, who identifies as Nepali in language, culture, tradition and spirit is a matter of individual and collective conscience, not a matter for Kathmandu to adjudicate. Neither media nor politicians hold the authority to tell a community that has carried its language, festivals and ancestry across centuries and continents that its identity is conditional or up for review.

articles.title: Fertiliser crisis is hitting farmers hard. Fix it
articles.summary:
A shortage of chemical fertiliser during the peak farming season has been a perennial problem in Nepal. It recurred this year as well. The government has all the information regarding the quantity the country needs, the timing of the demand, and the investment required to make fertilisers available at subsidised prices. Yet, it persistently fails to ensure their timely availability. As a result, farmers, mainly from Tarai, have to rely on the Indian market, fraught with legal risks.

India provides fertilisers—mainly Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP), urea and potash—to its farmers at subsidised rates. Under India’s Fertiliser (Control) Order and the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, subsidised fertiliser distributed for agricultural use cannot legally be exported or transported outside the country without authorisation. The law enables authorities to confiscate both the fertiliser and the vehicle used for transportation, while offenders can face imprisonment and fines.

Indian security forces have often been flexible in allowing Nepali farmers to bring in a few sacks of fertiliser. However, rising prices and shortages triggered by global tensions have prompted the Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar to tighten enforcement against attempts to supply fertiliser to Nepal. As a result, they are even making arrests, as recently happened to Nagendra Prasad Singh, 60, and Suresh Prasad Singh, 55, of Sarlahi district. The siblings, who were arrested in Sonbarsa, Bihar, remained behind bars for three weeks before the Nepal government started diplomatic dealings for their release.

Although it came late, the Foreign Ministry’s diplomatic initiative, which is expected to secure the release of the Singh brothers in a few days, is a welcome move. But that is not enough. Taking this as a lesson, the government should now focus on ensuring that no other Nepali citizen has to face what the Singh brothers endured. For that, chemical fertiliser should be made readily available to the nearly 60 percent of the population engaged in agriculture. Only then can the country permanently end the compulsion to depend on supplies from across the border.

Paddy production is not just a localised issue for farmers like the Singh brothers but a national concern, as it is directly linked to the country’s Gross Domestic Product. Better harvests contribute to higher economic growth, and fertiliser is one of the key inputs for increasing agricultural productivity. Nepali farmers are already struggling with several challenges. Less than half of the country’s agricultural land has irrigation facilities, leaving the rest dependent on rainfall. Erratic rainfall patterns caused by climate change have further compounded the problem. Expanding irrigation infrastructure is costly and time-consuming; climatic conditions are beyond anyone’s control.

One thing that any responsible government can address, however, is the timely availability of chemical fertiliser. This is possible through timely planning by assessing what volume of each type of fertiliser is needed and when. Successive governments have promised such planning but failed to deliver. As the present government came to power only about four months ago, it may not be appropriate to pin the blame on it. However, it cannot be excused if the same problem persists in the next planting season. The government’s ability to ensure the timely supply of fertiliser should be the basis for judging its performance.

articles.title: ‘Dialogue And Perception’ at Kala Salon
articles.summary:
